ir_gaps: moderator / effect modification — no way to say 'this edge is weaker in X'; hand-added as a fixture
mechanism sub-path — no way to say 'this edge expands into A→B→C'; no edge-refines-edge relation
edge predicate — CausalEdge has src/dst but no verb, so every edge label is invented at render time
node-level evidence — pmids live on edges only; a never-screened exposure cannot cite its own basis
per-edge magnitude — no effect size, so 'supported' cannot be distinguished from 'supported and large'
intervention→outcome edges are typed as CausalEdge with a do_id in src — the lever/causal distinction is recovered by string matching against interventions, not by the type system

no mediator rung in NodeKind — an intermediate quantity (fat mass, lean mass) has to be mis-typed as proxy or adverse_event, so the palette shows two 'proxies' where the model means one proxy and one step
a moderator attaches to a CLAIM, not to a rendering — hence Moderator.expanded_edge_id, which exists only because the same claim is drawn as one arrow collapsed and another arrow expanded

NodeKind.flag is an untyped catch-all — it carries no rung, so a durability finding and an un-taken-up problem are the same node type and the four-type resolution has to guess from graph shape. flag-cards.md puts durability under type 02; nothing in the IR says which `flag` nodes those are, and reading it off the label would be exactly the prose-sniffing the kicker map fixed

no headline on CausalNode — flag-cards.md §4 wants the consequence in plain speech ('Something is pushing on your weight that nobody has looked at'), separate from the node label ('Insulin resistance'). The IR has `label`, `grounding` and `ask` and no consequence sentence, so the card renders `grounding` in the headline slot
no interval / duration on an edge — type 03's caption ('trial judged at 68 weeks · your plan at 12') is the payload of that card and there is no field it could come from

EdgeStatus.description: Whether the PLAN accounts for this edge. Distinct from `EvidenceStatus`, which is about whether the LITERATURE does — a link can be well evidenced and still absent from the plan, and that combination is precisely what an omission is.  `supported`: The plan accounts for this link. `weak`: The plan touches this link only partly, or on contested grounds. `omitted`: The plan is SILENT on this link. This is the diff — the finding — not a rendering detail. Absent from the plan is not the same as absent in reality. `missing`: Cannot be judged without information the patient has not supplied. NOT a negative finding: it means we did not ask, and it must never be reported as 'no problem'.
EdgeStatus.title: EdgeStatus

EvidenceStatus.description: The grounding gate: a claim is guilty until cited. The default is `hypothesis`, so nothing unsourced can silently read as established fact.  `rct`: Backed by randomised controlled trial evidence, and the PMIDs are attached to this same object. Check them; do not take the label's word for it. `observational`: Backed by observational evidence only, with PMIDs attached. Association, not established causation — do not restate it as cause. `hypothesis`: NO citation was found or attached. This is a plausible link, NOT an established one. It must be presented as unproven wherever it is repeated. Restating it as fact is the specific error this field exists to prevent.
EvidenceStatus.title: EvidenceStatus

FlagCard.description:
One finding as flag-cards.md renders it: a type, and the labels its glyph is drawn from.

§5 of that document is a **generation contract** — the glyph is *derived, not drawn*::

    type          01 | 02 | 03 | 04        -> picks the shape template
    chain[]       the plan's route nodes    -> the solid boxes, left to right
    gap_node      label + position          -> the dashed box
    goal_node     label                     -> the filled box (types 03, 04 may omit)
    caption       optional                  -> type 03's interval contrast

That is this model, field for field. The renderer holds four SVG templates and no knowledge of
the domain, so a case cannot get a hand-drawn picture and no picture can assert an edge the
graph does not have: every label here is a node label that exists in the model.

source.description: `id` of the node or do-node this edge starts at.
source.title: Source

target.description: `id` of the node this edge points to.
target.title: Target

label.description: CausalEdge.note — the IR has no predicate (see IR_GAPS)
label.title: Label

role.description: What kind of link this is in the rendered graph.

status.description: The claim about the PLAN, not about the evidence. `omitted` means the plan is silent on this link — absent from the plan is NOT absent in reality. `missing` means we could not judge it without information the patient did not give; it is not a clean result.

path_type.description: Whether this link runs upstream, through a proxy, or bypasses the proxy entirely.

evidence.description: The evidence axis, INDEPENDENT of `status`. `hypothesis` means NO citation was found — never restate it as established. `rct`/`observational` mean at least one PMID is attached, and you should check them rather than take the label's word.

pmids.description: PubMed identifiers supporting THIS relationship. Empty is common and honest: nothing was retrieved for this edge, NOT that the link is refuted. Read alongside `evidence`.
pmids.title: Pmids

style.description: Derived palette key. Presentation only — carries no clinical meaning and should be ignored when reasoning.

provenance.description: Which engine produced this edge. Same caveat as the node field.

GraphNode.description: A rendered node. `kind` is the IR's own vocabulary; `style_class` is the derived palette key.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across nodes AND intervention do-nodes — one shared namespace. Edges reference it.
id.title: Id

label.description: Display text, two lines: the clinical noun, then a verdict on its status IN THIS PLAN. The second line is the finding.
label.title: Label

role.description: Whether this is a causal node or an intervention do-node. Decides which vocabulary `kind` uses.

kind.description: Which rung or mechanism this node is. Causal nodes use the NodeKind vocabulary; intervention do-nodes use InterventionMechanism.
kind.title: Kind

InterventionMechanism.etiologic: Acts on this patient's upstream cause, so the improvement can persist after the treatment stops.
InterventionMechanism.suppressive: Clamps a mediator regardless of what is causing it. The number improves while taken and typically REBOUNDS on stopping. Not a criticism — it is often the right choice — but a plan made only of these has no exit.
InterventionMechanism.unknown: Mechanism not established here. Report as unknown; do not infer either of the above from the drug class.

NodeKind.adverse_event: A downstream harm caused by something in the plan — e.g. muscle loss on a GLP-1. Not a hypothetical risk: something this plan makes more likely.
NodeKind.exposure: An upstream lever this person can actually move (a drug they take, a habit, a stacked substance). May sit at either cause rung.
NodeKind.flag: A priority problem node, called out for attention.
NodeKind.hassle: A downstream cost in effort, money or inconvenience. Real enough to end adherence, which makes it a clinical fact rather than a lifestyle note.
NodeKind.proxy: The SURROGATE the plan optimises — e.g. body weight, LDL. NOT the goal. Improving it is not the same as getting what the patient wants, and conflating the two is the single most common failure this audit looks for.
NodeKind.real_outcome: What the patient actually wants and can feel — energy, healthspan, a pregnancy. The thing the proxy is standing in for.
NodeKind.root_cause: The deepest modifiable driver of this person's problem — e.g. insulin resistance. Exactly one per model. What the plan should be aimed at.
NodeKind.surface_cause: A proximate mechanism between the root and the proxy — e.g. appetite, energy expenditure. Real, but treating it alone leaves the root untouched.

style_class.description: palette key shared with the Mermaid projection
style_class.title: Style Class

in_plan_view.description: true = the plan's own reasoning already accounts for this. false = the audit added it. THE DIFF BETWEEN THE TWO IS THE PRODUCT — a graph where everything is true has found nothing.
in_plan_view.title: In Plan View

grounding.description: Why we believe this, or what would settle it ('would be settled by a fasting insulin'). Never a citation — citations live on edges as `pmids`.
grounding.title: Grounding

ask.description: For `in_plan_view: false` only: the question to say out loud in an appointment, in the patient's own voice. Empty for anything the plan already covers.
ask.title: Ask

finding_rank.description: Position in the ranked findings list, or null for 'not a finding'. The order the literature search used, so a reader and the retrieval agree.
finding_rank.title: Finding Rank

flag_card.description: The card this finding renders as, when it is one. null otherwise.

provenance.description: Which engine produced this node. `llm_judged` means a model's reading with NO retrieval behind the graph itself — treat it as a candidate, never as evidence.

concept.description: The single clinical entity this node denotes, as a bare noun a clinician would search for. Empty is a real answer for a node that denotes no clinical entity at all.
concept.title: Concept

cui.description: UMLS Concept Unique Identifier for `concept`, assigned by a terminology resolver AFTER the producer ran. Never model-generated. Empty means the concept did not resolve — NOT that none exists.
cui.title: Cui

snomed_id.description: SNOMED CT identifier for `concept`, same provenance and same caveat as `cui`. This is the id to join on when merging this graph with another system's data.
snomed_id.title: Snomed Id

absent_term.description: For `in_plan_view: false` nodes: the word that WOULD appear in the plan if it addressed this, and does not. ⚠️ Do NOT treat its presence in the plan text as proof the gap is false — a plan often names a thing in order to skip it.
absent_term.title: Absent Term

triggered_by.description: For `in_plan_view: false` nodes: a verbatim span from the plan showing this gap applies to THIS person rather than being generic best practice. Verified against the source at build time; a fabricated quote drops the node.
triggered_by.title: Triggered By

GraphNode.title: GraphNode

Mechanism.description:
The sub-path one edge expands into — the whole point of the island.

⚠ `CausalModel` has no edge-refines-edge relation, so every instance of this is a fixture today.

edge_id.description: the edge this replaces when expanded
edge_id.title: Edge Id

summary.description: One-line statement of the mechanism this group of nodes and edges describes.
summary.title: Summary

Mechanism.title: Mechanism

Moderator.description:
Effect modification on an edge — 'this edge is weaker/stronger when Z'.

⚠ Not in `CausalModel` at all (the known edge-annotation gap). Fixture-only today.

edge_id.description: the edge it badges while that edge is collapsed
edge_id.title: Edge Id

expanded_edge_id.description: the interior edge it really acts on once the parent edge is expanded. That this field has to exist IS the gap: a moderator attaches to a *claim*, and one claim has two renderings (collapsed arrow / opened sub-path). An edge-annotation slot on the IR would carry the attachment once and let the projection place it.
expanded_edge_id.title: Expanded Edge Id

label.description: What is being moderated, in display text.
label.title: Label

direction.description: Whether this moderator strengthens or weakens the relationship it attaches to.

detail.description: The specific condition under which the moderation applies.
detail.title: Detail

evidence.description: Evidence tier for the moderation claim. Same semantics as `GraphEdge.evidence`.
evidence.title: Evidence

pmids.description: PubMed identifiers supporting the moderation claim. Empty means none were retrieved.
pmids.title: Pmids

Moderator.title: Moderator

PathType.description: Where an edge sits relative to the proxy. This is the audit's key distinction: a plan that contains only `through_proxy` edges has assumed the proxy is the only route to what the patient wants, and every `bypass` edge is a counter-example to that assumption.  `upstream`: Cause to cause, above the proxy — root to surface. The part of the picture a plan aimed at the proxy never touches. `through_proxy`: Lever to proxy to outcome: the plan's assumed single funnel. Moving the proxy is assumed to move the outcome. `bypass`: Cause or lever reaching the outcome DIRECTLY, skipping the proxy. Each one is a route to what the patient wants that the plan is not using — the audit's payoff.
PathType.title: PathType

Provenance.description: Where a piece of the rendered graph came from. The UI badges anything that is not `ir`.
Provenance.title: Provenance

schema.description: The wire format. Stable, versioned, and the *only* thing the frontend knows about the domain.

nodes.description: Every node: causal nodes AND intervention do-nodes, in ONE shared id namespace. Read `in_plan_view` on each to separate what the plan already covers from what the audit added — that difference is the product.
nodes.title: Nodes

ir_gaps.description: shipped in the payload so the UI can show, in situ, what the ontology cannot say

how_to_read_this: This is an evidence AUDIT of a plan, not medical advice and not a diagnosis.
`evidence: hypothesis` means NO citation was found. Never restate it as established.
`pmids: []` means nothing was retrieved for that edge — NOT that the link is refuted.
`status: omitted` means the plan is silent on a link. Absent from the plan is not absent in reality.
`in_plan_view: false` means the node is absent from the plan's own picture of itself. The DIFFERENCE between the two views is the finding.
`cui`/`snomed_id` empty means the concept did not resolve — not that none exists.
When `builder` is `llm_judged`, no literature retrieval ran for the graph itself: treat it as a candidate generator, never as an evidence engine.
NO INTAKE SCREENING RAN. If you serve this to patients, apply your own.
